kept.excerpt: Asked about the future of negotiations with the US, Gharibabadi said on Saturday that Iran had been engaged in talks when Washington breached its commitments under the Islamabad memorandum of understanding by launching acts of aggression. "We have also suspended our commitments under the Islamabad memorandum of understanding and are no longer implementing them," he stated. "If they are wise, they should choose other solutions," Gharibabadi said.
kept.relevance: The deputy foreign minister's latest statement explicitly describes suspended implementation, making its precise wording central to distinguishing a suspension from definitive termination of participation.

kept.excerpt: Iran’s parliament speaker and lead negotiator said the country is not declaring last month’s interim deal void. Mohammad Bagher Qalibaf said Iran’s commitment depends on continued implementation by the United States. If Washington fails to honor its obligations, Iran would have no reason to remain bound by it, he argued.
kept.relevance: Iran's lead negotiator expressly preserved the agreement while making a conditional warning, which is directly relevant to the resolution's exclusion of conditional withdrawal.

kept.excerpt: Mediators from countries that include Pakistan, Qatar and Egypt have been working to resume talks, according to regional officials who spoke on condition of anonymity to discuss the sensitive diplomacy. They noted that neither side has notified Pakistan that it was officially withdrawing or terminating the initial ceasefire agreement. The regional officials acknowledged that the 60-day negotiating process spelled out in the interim deal has halted.
kept.relevance: Mediator reporting distinguishes a halted negotiating process from formal withdrawal and supplies evidence that diplomatic efforts remained active shortly before the cutoff.

kept.excerpt: Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei accused Washington on Monday of driving the MoU "into crisis", saying Washington has consistently violated its commitments. The MoU says Washington and Tehran commit to negotiating a final deal in a maximum of 60 days, extendable by mutual consent. With control over the Strait of Hormuz contested, the sides have not declared any date for further talks.
kept.publisher: Reuters, published by The Irish Times
kept.relevance: This identifies the official Iranian complaint and absence of a scheduled next round without equating either with a definitive announcement ending participation.

kept.excerpt: The US has denied Iranian accusations that it hit civilian infrastructure in the latest wave of air strikes since peace talks collapsed. The BBC has confirmed an attack on a bridge in Hormozgan province. President Donald Trump has threatened to hit Iranian bridges and power stations to force Tehran to return to talks to end the war.
kept.relevance: Renewed attacks and pressure to return to talks describe the immediate escalation backdrop that could influence Iran's subsequent official negotiating position.

kept.excerpt: Iran’s Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said the country will not enter further negotiations for a final agreement until key provisions of a memorandum of understanding are implemented. Qatar said that technical talks between Iran and the United States are continuing, although no high-level meetings are currently taking place under the existing negotiation framework. Foreign Ministry spokesperson Majed Al Ansari said technical contacts had continued through both direct and indirect channels.
kept.relevance: The contrasting Iranian and mediator accounts establish an earlier pattern of conditional refusal alongside continuing technical contacts, relevant to interpreting later suspension language.

kept.excerpt: The United States of America and the Islamic Republic of Iran commit to negotiating and achieving the final deal in maximum 60 days, extendable with mutual consent. After signing this MoU and subject to the beginning of the implementation of paragraphs 1, 4, 5, 10 and 11 of this MoU and the continuing implementation of these measures, the United States of America and the Islamic Republic of Iran will start negotiations regarding the final deal exclusively on the other paragraphs.
kept.relevance: The published MOU text establishes the negotiation window and implementation prerequisites underlying Iranian objections and demands for compliance.

search_notes: Frozen cutoff: 2026-07-18. All included sources display publication dates on or before that date; later-dated reporting, retrospective outcome material, prediction-market pages, odds and prices were excluded. The two July 16 AP entries are the same syndicated article and constitute one reporting source, included separately to preserve distinct relevant excerpts; they are not independent corroboration. Dates and excerpts were verified using web_search-indexed source text. Full-page web_fetch failed because of a provider-configuration error, and the requested agent-reach web read fallback returned RATE_LIMITED, so full-page retrieval was unavailable. Sources distinguish the June 14 announcement from the June 17 signing and publication of the MOU. The supplied resolution text is truncated, and no missing language was inferred. Suspension of commitments, halted talks and conditional warnings have been preserved as such rather than treated as definitive termination.
